body.text: The primary purpose of the NFP is to mitigate the effects of fire within and around the NI facilities.

body.text: NNA strategy is to mitigate the effects of a sodium fire once a leak has occurred. Leak prevention is outside its scope.
body.anchor: Leak prevention is outside the scope of NNA

body.text: The Fire Protection Program and Fire Hazards Analysis will be provided at the operating license stage.

body.text: Fire water comes from the Energy Island Fire Protection System (EFP).
body.anchor: The water supply to the NFD is from the Energy Island Fire Protection System

body.text: There are two fire water storage tanks with a minimum of 300,000 gallons each. Either can be refilled in 8 hours or less.
body.anchor: with a minimum of 300,000 gallons each

body.text: There are two fire pumps: a primary electric motor pump and a backup diesel engine driven pump.
body.anchor: a primary electric motor pump and a backup diesel engine driven pump

body.text: A jockey pump keeps required pressure in normal conditions.
body.anchor: A jockey pump is also installed in the system

body.text: The pumps have a 3-hour fire rated separation.
body.anchor: a 3-hour fire rated separation between the pumps

concepts.title: Suppression and where water is kept out

body.text: Water-based suppression is in buildings where sodium is not present.
body.anchor: The water-based suppression systems are located in buildings where sodium is not present

body.text: The RXB and RAB contain sodium, are not sprinklered, and do not contain fire water.
body.anchor: are the Reactor Building and the Reactor Auxiliary Building

body.text: The FHB contains sodium but has separated sprinklered areas, such as radwaste handling areas and truck bays.
body.anchor: such as radwaste handling areas and truck bays

body.text: Preaction systems are used where water-filled piping is not desirable.
body.anchor: are used where water-filled piping is not desirable

body.text: Clean agent systems serve areas where water would be detrimental.
body.anchor: are located where fire suppression is required but water would be detrimental

body.text: Four independent clean agent systems serve the NCB substructure, one for each RPS division.
body.anchor: There are four independent clean agent systems in the NI Control Building substructure

body.text: Class D extinguishers are in areas containing sodium.
body.anchor: Class D fire extinguishers are provided in areas containing sodium

body.text: NFA has initiation devices, notification appliances, control equipment, and wiring.
body.anchor: consists of initiation devices

body.text: Each building has its own Fire Alarm Control Panel. Panels are networked to the NFA workstation in the MCR.
body.anchor: Each building has its own Fire Alarm Control Panel

body.text: NFA and NNA have internal batteries for when power is not available.
body.anchor: The NFA has internal system storage batteries

body.text: Normal NFP operation is standby.
body.anchor: Normal system operation is standby mode

body.text: When smoke is detected in a duct, the NHV air handling unit shuts down and local smoke dampers close.
body.anchor: When smoke is detected in a duct, the associated NHV air handling unit is shut down

body.text: NFA also has trouble and supervisory modes.
body.anchor: The NFA also has trouble and supervisory modes

body.text: Sprinklers activate individually at their temperature, and clean agent systems activate on a signal from the NFA.

body.text: NNA detects leaked sodium, collects it, and drains it to catch pans, while giving operators early notice.
body.anchor: giving operators early notification of a leak so they can take necessary action

body.text: The overall strategy uses passive features and adds active ones only where necessary.
body.anchor: The overall sodium fire strategy is to use passive prevention and mitigation features
